approval_required_for: Conditional bounded approval is required only if fresh exact-board discovery yields multiple fully evidenced compatible Vivado cell/wrapper candidates; the approval must bind the selected cell, wrapper source hash, recursive simulation closure, and AXI compatibility. No approval is currently requested.

consumes: failed selector history record as diagnostic-only evidence
current user-supplied sample-project source inventory and recursive simulation closure
executable_actions.on_failure: Keep board simulation, RTL repair, backend work, and promotion blocked. If semantic binding or closure validation fails, record a current verification-capability failure and repeat only this discovery repair with a newly immutable record. If multiple fully evidenced compatible cell/wrapper candidates remain, produce the ambiguity report required by repair.board_target_ambiguity_approval; do not select one implicitly.
executable_actions.rationale: Repair the first executed board-layer blocker by creating a new immutable selector interpretation bound to its semantic checkpoint chunk and by rerunning discovery against real Vivado facts and the exact user-supplied sample-project source closure. This action must identify a real cell object, a wrapper source contained in the recursive simulation closure, cited source hashes, and required AXI compatibility; it must not guess names or substitute a simplified wrapper.

consumes: current Vivado cell facts and source hashes
executable_actions.on_failure: Leave case_board_interface_discovery and all dependent board gates blocked; do not generate a testbench or compile plan for an unapproved ambiguous target.
executable_actions.rationale: This action is executable only if the fresh discovery result contains more than one fully cited candidate that passes closure and AXI compatibility checks. The board-integration engineer must obtain a bounded decision identifying the approved Vivado cell, wrapper source hash, and source closure rather than guessing a board target.

consumes: current immutable target checkpoint and complete target-layer Transformer-block tensor catalog inputs
current immutable numeric policy and tolerance
current generated DUT loader and memory runtime artifacts
executable_actions.on_failure: Classify missing catalog coverage, target reference, exact wrapper binding, generated testbench hash, compile authority, or DUT weight-consumption proof as a current verification/harness repair. Do not execute a fallback testbench, obtain expected values from RTL, alter numeric tolerances, or reopen lower-layer certificates.
executable_actions.rationale: After exact board identity is valid, construct the missing board testbench and simulation authority from that exact wrapper closure. Rebuild complete-scope, hash-bound Transformer-block tensor coverage across required target layers; bind the loader/harness to the DUT; and derive expected outputs by executing the real target model on the unchanged checkpoint and stimulus. Preserve the current numeric comparison policy and exclude embedding/tokenization, final norm, LM head/logits, sampling, and all other model-tail work.

consumes: current immutable numeric policy and tolerance
executable_actions.on_failure: If a prerequisite checker fails, return to the corresponding discovery or semantic-harness repair and do not claim RTL failure. If a real simulator or protocol run fails, preserve its logs and invoke repair.localize_current_board_trace_before_patch; do not proceed to synthesis, implementation, bitstream, runtime, or board execution.
executable_actions.rationale: With discovery and semantic-harness prerequisites repaired, execute the required board-layer checks in dependency order using the exact selected wrapper and immutable semantic contract. This establishes the first admissible current board functional/AXI/DDR evidence and, on a real failure, the trace needed for causal localization. Passing this action returns a Stage7 candidate only; it does not promote to backend or runtime.

consumes: connected-kernel timing evidence with contract SHA-256 496fc6b3c907d9401a2156dc906f39f7a7ade964fa60f682fff0be5f31b5b393
executable_actions.on_failure: Do not patch an inferred downstream module or reopen lower layers. Increase only current-board trace observability and rerun the exact current wrapper/harness. If the trace explicitly contradicts a named lower-layer invariant, create a scoped backtrack request naming the contradicted module, boundary, certificate hash, and trace evidence; otherwise restrict subsequent repair to the board wrapper/runtime/integration slice.
produces: conditional lower-layer contradiction record or explicit no-lower-layer-challenge record
executable_actions.rationale: Execute only when the fresh board rerun produces a real functional, ordering, AXI, DDR, or liveness failure. Localize the earliest causal board boundary using accepted input handshakes, core start, ingress, egress, named causal boundaries, output/lifecycle frontier, and current certificate hashes. A frontier stall is localization evidence only, not a root-cause or pass claim. The certified elastic kernel is reopened only if this trace directly contradicts its named boundary-order or overlap invariant.

executable_actions.on_failure: Keep every existing barrier and retry request active, retain the candidate as planning/debug evidence only, and route back to the failed current-layer action. Do not promote to backend synthesis, implementation, bitstream, runtime ABI, or board runtime.
produces: updated SACG blocker and retry state
executable_actions.rationale: A fresh candidate may supersede prior same-scope retry artifacts only after all current board gates and semantic evidence pass with content-addressed outputs. This action preserves the active contamination barriers and open retry requests as downstream-consumption blockers until checker-backed reconciliation; it does not manually clear historical records and does not authorize backend promotion.

observations: The current scope is board_axi_ddr_wrapped_system. Certified lower layers remain live and hash-bound: operator-leaf certificate SHA-256 2bbc6880205155cbc1119882b2503281c2cb43b4b3c0d40a1754acb1e3a20569 and single-layer certificate SHA-256 44d3689d835f165fd30e794aeec2dabf648d1d65d17a24a53d3a6aac6e3854e7. No current trace challenges either certificate.

The only executed current-scope real-tool failure is case_board_interface_discovery. Its selector was unbound to its semantic checkpoint chunk, produced no Vivado cell fact, selected no wrapper inside the sample simulation closure, and did not establish the required 512-bit AXI compute-slot compatibility.

functional_sim=fail is not evidence of a board RTL value, liveness, ordering, AXI, or DDR fault. Its preconditions are missing board_tb.sv and prerequisite board gates; VCS functional simulation, evidence analysis, and deadlock/AXI analysis are not_run.

The historical VCS diagnosis reporting zero accepted kernel-output beats is explicitly historical_only and unbound to the present board layer, failed gate, and live source artifacts. It cannot localize a repair or reopen the connected kernel.

The board source identity, board testbench, full multi-layer Transformer-block binding proof, board semantic evidence, AXI/DDR simulation authority, and board functional trace must be rebuilt from the exact selected sample-project wrapper. Model-tail operations remain outside this DUT, tensor-coverage, and golden boundary.

SACG truth reports eight active same-scope contamination barriers and three open same-scope retry requests. Rejected Stage7/Stage8 artifacts may guide repair but cannot be used as validated inputs or promotion evidence. There are no active same-scope backtrack requests.
The conditional design-team router made no specialist split because the failure class is unambiguous. That routing outcome does not replace the failed real-tool evidence or relax any checker.
proposed_actions: Reissue board-interface discovery using a newly immutable, semantically bound selector record and current exact Vivado/sample-project evidence; do not reuse the unbound selector record or infer a target from filenames.
If and only if discovery yields multiple fully evidenced eligible cells/wrappers, obtain bounded human selection approval rather than guessing; otherwise continue with the uniquely evidenced target.

Generate the missing board_tb.sv and board simulation manifest from the selected exact wrapper closure, while rebuilding complete Transformer-block weight-binding and target-model semantic evidence without altering frozen inputs, tolerance, or golden policy.

Run the board-layer gate DAG in dependency order. Only after discovery, binding, and AXI/DDR preconditions pass may VCS, trace analysis, deadlock/AXI checking, semantic assembly, and numeric comparison run.

If the new real simulation fails, localize its earliest board boundary through a current trace and targeted replay. Repair only that identified wrapper/runtime/integration slice; lower-layer revalidation is conditional on direct contradiction of named certificate evidence.

Retain all existing barriers and retries until SACG observes a fresh all-pass board candidate. A successful candidate must reconcile, rather than manually erase, the prior retry and contamination records.
risks: Guessing a cell, wrapper, module, path, or AXI width without cited Vivado and recursive simulation-closure evidence would violate the exact-board-wrapper requirement and could bind a simplified substitute.

A board testbench that lacks a complete Transformer-block tensor catalog, loader-to-DUT consumption evidence, immutable checkpoint/stimulus provenance, target-model reference outputs, or frozen numeric policy would not support a functional pass.

Changing atol, rtol, max_mismatch_fraction, checkpoint, stimulus, target reference, golden output, or wrapper/source hashes during repair would contaminate comparison evidence; random stimulus is permitted only if its provenance is fixed, and expected values must remain target-model-derived.

Model configuration, tensor shape/layout, token/data order, DDR addresses, loader timing, AXI protocol, lifecycle progress, and output comparison must remain mutually bound. Independent prefetch or AXI activity does not establish output-frontier progress.

The connected kernel is certified as an elastic variable-latency token pipeline. Unequal stage timing is not a failure by itself; only a current trace contradicting its verified boundary order or required cross-token overlap can justify a lower-layer backtrack.

The active contamination barriers and retry requests block downstream consumption and promotion until a fresh, content-addressed current-scope candidate passes all required board gates and is reconciled by SACG.
